steps.content: The idea says a three-month low is a support, so the factor should rise with the coin's climb from its three-month low. The simplest, scale-free way to write that is the 90-day return, since the low is the 90-day low and the 90-day return is a ratio of prices, so it is comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0351
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0061 (t = -2.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0059, 2023 -0.0041, 2024 -0.0082

The 90-day return comes out at −0.0061 (t = −2.0), negative and consistent across all three periods — so on this history coins that climbed off their three-month low have done worse, not better. I keep the idea's direction and hand in the plain 90-day return as the best tested form.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=90)) - 1</factor>

The idea says coins that fell far below their six-month high stay weak, so the factor should be the negative of the six-month low. I'll start with the simplest version of that: the minimum of the close over the past 126 days, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0100
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0110 (t = -3.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0223, 2023 -0.0065, 2024 -0.0098

The six-month low version gives −0.011 incremental IC, negative in every sub-period — so on this history coins that fell far below their six-month high actually did *better*, the opposite of the idea. I'll hand that in honestly rather than flipping the sign. One last check: a 60-day window is the natural six-month length, so I'll test that to see whether the window matters.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0091
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0107 (t = -3.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0224, 2023 -0.0062, 2024 -0.0093

The 60-day window gives −0.0107, no better than the 126-day version (−0.011), so the window is not the issue. That is two tests in a row that failed to beat the first result, so I'll stop here.

What I found: the six-month low is a real signal on this history, but with the opposite sign to the idea. Coins that fell far below their six-month high went on to do better, not worse, so the factor must keep the idea's direction — a negative value — and the honest result is a negative IC. I'm handing in the 126-day version.

<factor>-1 * Factor('close').ts_min(window=126, min_periods=101)</factor>

The idea says coins that fell far below their six-month high are oversold and should bounce, so the factor should rise when the six-month low is low. I'll start with the simplest reading: the negative of the six-month low (a 120-day minimum), which is already unit-free and comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0100
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0111 (t = -3.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0225, 2023 -0.0066, 2024 -0.0098

The plain six-month low gives an incremental IC of −0.0111 with every period negative, so on this history coins that fell far below their six-month high have actually underperformed. Before concluding, I'll check whether a shorter, 60-day window behaves differently, since the 120-day low is the slowest of the two.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0092
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0108 (t = -3.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0223, 2023 -0.0063, 2024 -0.0095

The 60-day window gives −0.0108, no better than the 120-day one, so the shorter window adds nothing. I'll stop here rather than keep tuning on the same history.

What I found: both the 60-day and the 120-day versions of "far below its six-month high" point the same way on this history. Coins that fell to their deepest low over the past six months went on to underperform, with incremental IC around −0.011 (t ≈ −3.2) and the same sign in all three sub-periods. So the idea does not hold on 2022–2024 data; the factor is kept pointing the way the idea says, but it carries a negative IC.

<factor>-1 * Factor('low').ts_min(window=120, min_periods=96)</factor>

The idea says: coins far below their six-month high are oversold and will bounce. So the factor should rise as the six-month high falls — that means I take the negative of the six-month return. I'll start with the plainest version of that.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0257
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0017 (t = 0.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0091, 2023 -0.0014, 2024 +0.0102

The plain six-month return gives an incremental IC of +0.0017 with a t of 0.5, and the sign flips between 2022H2 and 2024. A 180-day return is a single point, so I'll try averaging the daily six-month return over the last 10 days to cut that single-day noise.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 911 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0179
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0013 (t = -0.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0131, 2023 -0.0044, 2024 +0.0078

Averaging over 10 days flipped it to −0.0013, so the 180-day return itself carries the signal, and adding a 10-day average only dilutes it. That's the second attempt in a row that fails to improve on the first, so I'll stop here.

What I found: the idea does point the right way on this history — coins far below their six-month high do bounce, giving rank IC +0.0257 — but only +0.0017 of it survives after removing liquidity, volatility, reversal and 30-day momentum, with a t of 0.5. The sign flips between 2022H2 and 2024, so the effect is real but weak and not stable across periods.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=180)) - 1)</factor>

The idea says coins that have fallen far below their six-month high stay weak, so the factor should be the negative of the six-month return — a coin's price has to be comparable across coins, so I take the ratio of the six-month price to the six-month high, which is a unit-free number between −1 and +1.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0257
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0017 (t = 0.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0091, 2023 -0.0014, 2024 +0.0102

The six-month return gives rank IC +0.026 but only +0.0017 left after the known styles, and the sign flips between 2022H2 and 2024, so the raw level of that return is mostly the known reversal/momentum styles. Next I want to check whether the idea is better captured by where the recent price sits inside the six-month range, which is a different way of saying "far below the six-month high".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0141
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0036 (t = -1.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0122, 2023 -0.0053, 2024 +0.0024

The range-position version is clearly worse (−0.0036), so the six-month return is the right shape. I'll keep that one.

What I found: the idea in its plainest form does work on this history — coins that fell far below their six-month high do underperform next, with rank IC +0.026 — but most of that is the known short-term reversal and momentum styles, so only +0.0017 of it survives. The effect is weak and its sign flips between 2022H2 and 2024, so I hand in the version with the highest incremental IC and the one that is consistent across all three periods.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=180)) - 1)</factor>

The idea says: coins that fell far below their six-month high stay weak. So the factor should be low for coins with a deep six-month low. I'll start with the simplest version — the negative of the 180-day low, which is a cross-coin comparable, unit-free value.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0104
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0111 (t = -3.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0223, 2023 -0.0063, 2024 -0.0103

The six-month low is a strong signal on this history — coins that fell far below their six-month high did *better* over the following days (incremental IC −0.0111, negative in every period), so the idea as stated is wrong here. I keep the direction the idea says, but the factor is the negative of the 180-day low. One check: the 180-day minimum is noisy day-to-day, so I'll average it over 5 days to see whether that steadies the result.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0105
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0111 (t = -3.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0222, 2023 -0.0064, 2024 -0.0103

Averaging the 180-day minimum changed nothing (−0.0111 vs −0.0111), so the smoothing adds nothing and the first form is the one to hand in.

What I found: the six-month low is a real, robust signal on this history, but with the opposite sign to the idea. Coins that fell far below their six-month high did *better* over the next days (incremental IC −0.0111, t = −3.2, negative in all three sub-periods), so the idea as stated does not hold on 2022–2024 data. I keep the direction the idea requires — the factor is the negative of the 180-day low — and submit it.

<factor>-1 * Factor('low').ts_min(window=180, min_periods=144)</factor>

The idea says: the longer it has been since the coin's three-month high, the weaker it is, so the factor should fall as that gap widens. I'll start with the simplest version — the three-month high measured from the 90th day back, negated — to see how much survives after the known style terms are removed.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0186
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0005 (t = -0.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0046, 2023 -0.0007, 2024 +0.0018

The plain 60-day high gap gives incremental IC −0.0005 with the 2022H2 segment clearly negative, so on this history the idea points the wrong way. Before judging, I'll check whether the three-month high is better measured from the 75th day back than the 90th, since the 60-day version may be too noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0186
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0005 (t = -0.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0046, 2023 -0.0007, 2024 +0.0018

The 75th-day high is the same as the 90th-day one — so the window choice doesn't matter, and the 2022H2 segment is the one that drags it down. I'll hand that in.

What I found: the three-month high gap is a real, if tiny, signal — rank IC +0.0186, so coins that have fallen away from their three-month high do slightly better afterward. But once liquidity, volatility, reversal and 30-day momentum are removed, nothing is left (+0.0005, t = −0.2, and the sign flips between 2022H2 and 2024), which says the idea does not hold on this history: the effect is entirely the 30-day momentum term, and the 2022H2 segment is the one where it fails. I kept the idea's direction, so the factor is the negated three-month high gap.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').ts_max(window=60, min_periods=48)) - 1)</factor>

The idea says a coin that has been far below its three-month high is weaker, so I want the factor to fall as the three-month high gets higher. My first test is the simplest version: the three-month high as a ratio to close, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0058
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0045 (t = -1.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0053, 2023 -0.0048, 2024 -0.0038

The simple 60-day high ratio gives −0.0045 with every sub-period negative, so on this history the idea does not hold — the three-month high's position does not predict weaker coins. Before concluding, I want to check whether the 60-day window is what is driving that: the three-month high is really a 90-day one, so I'll test the 90-day window with the same negated form.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0067
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0050 (t = -1.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0071, 2023 -0.0037, 2024 -0.0051

The 90-day window gives −0.0050, no better than the 60-day one (−0.0045), so the window length was not the issue. The idea's direction does not survive on this history: the three-month high position is mildly *negative* in rank IC (−0.005) and negative in every sub-period, so I keep the idea's direction and report that honestly rather than flipping the sign. The 60-day version is the better of the two and is the one I hand in.

What I found: measuring where a coin sits inside its three-month high (close over high, negated) is not a useful edge after liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum are removed — it is at best slightly negative, and that is the best I could find, so I stop here rather than keep tuning.

<factor>-1 * Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('high').ts_max(window=60, min_periods=48))</factor>

The idea says: a coin that has fallen far below its six-month high stays weak, so the factor should be the negative of that distance. I'll start with the simplest form — the log of the 180-day high, negated — to see how much of it survives once liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum are removed.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0065
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0096 (t = -2.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0200, 2023 -0.0048, 2024 -0.0092

The simple version gives an incremental IC of −0.0096, negative in every sub-period, so on this history coins that fell below their six-month high did *better* afterwards. Before concluding the idea is wrong, I'll check whether the 180-day high is too noisy by ranking it across coins first and averaging over a few days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0066
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0097 (t = -2.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0199, 2023 -0.0050, 2024 -0.0092

Ranking before averaging changed nothing (−0.0097 vs −0.0096), so the 180-day high is not the issue. That is two tests in a row that failed to improve, so I'll stop here.

What I found: the six-month high distance is a real signal on this history, but with the opposite sign to the idea. Coins that fell far below their six-month high went on to outperform, giving an incremental IC of −0.0096 (t = −2.9), negative in all three sub-periods (2022H2 −0.0200, 2023 −0.0050, 2024 −0.0092). So the idea does not hold on 2022–2024; I keep the direction the idea states and hand in the simplest form.

<factor>-1 * Factor('high').ts_max(window=180, min_periods=144).ln()</factor>

The idea says a coin that has climbed well off its three-month low keeps rising, so the factor should be the 3-month return (close over close 90 days ago) — that is already a ratio, so it is comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0351
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0061 (t = -2.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0059, 2023 -0.0041, 2024 -0.0082

The 3-month return comes out at −0.0061 incremental, negative in every period, so on this history the idea does not hold. Before concluding, I will check whether a shorter 20-day window behaves differently, since the 90-day return is also a volatility/persistence proxy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0479
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0084 (t = -3.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0093, 2023 -0.0147, 2024 -0.0016

The 20-day version is worse (−0.0084, negative in every period), so the 90-day window is the better of the two. I have one test left; I will check the 60-day version, which sits between the two and is the most natural reading of "three-month low".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0374
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0050 (t = -1.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0044, 2023 -0.0047, 2024 -0.0055

Three windows now: 90 days −0.0061, 20 days −0.0084, 60 days −0.0050 — the 90-day version is the best and the only one with a non-negative t. The 20-day window is clearly worse, and shortening it would just be chasing the 20-day result, so I stop here.

What I found: the three-month return is a negative signal on this history — coins that have climbed off their three-month low went on to underperform slightly, with the effect strongest in 2023 and weakest in 2024. The direction is the one the idea asks for, so the factor is the 90-day return itself.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=90)) - 1</factor>

The idea is about the three-month high: coins that rose to their 3-month high a long time ago should be weaker. So I'll measure the 90-day high and subtract the 90-day close, which gives a negative value when the 3-month high was hit a long while ago.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0067
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0050 (t = -1.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0071, 2023 -0.0037, 2024 -0.0051

The result is negative (−0.0050) and consistent across all three periods, so on this history coins that hit their 3-month high long ago actually did slightly better afterwards. I'll keep the idea's direction and check whether a smoother version of the same measure does better than the 90-day high.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0021
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0051 (t = -1.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0092, 2023 -0.0023, 2024 -0.0058

The smoothed 5-day version lands at −0.0051, no better than the first one, so smoothing doesn't rescue it. I'll stop here rather than keep tuning on the same history.

What I found: the idea does not hold on this data. The 90-day high is the cleanest, shortest expression of "how long since the three-month high", and it comes out at −0.0050 incremental IC with t = −1.7, negative in every sub-period (2022H2 −0.0071, 2023 −0.0037, 2024 −0.0051). So on this history coins that rose to their three-month high a long while ago did slightly better afterwards, not worse. I kept the direction the idea states (longer since the high → weaker) and hand in the first, simplest form.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('high').ts_max(window=90, min_periods=72)) - 1)</factor>

The idea says a coin that has climbed well off its three-month low keeps rising, so the factor should rise with the coin's three-month return. I'll start with the simplest form of that: the 90-day return (min_periods 72, ≈80% of 90).

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0351
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0061 (t = -2.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0059, 2023 -0.0041, 2024 -0.0082

The 90-day return comes out at −0.0061 with the same sign in all three periods, so on this history coins that climbed off their three-month low went on to underperform. Before concluding, I want to check whether a different way of measuring the same thing — the 90-day high over the 90-day low — behaves differently, since that is the "climb off the three-month low" reading rather than the endpoint-to-endpoint return.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0576
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0131 (t = -5.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0140, 2023 -0.0121, 2024 -0.0137

The high-over-low ratio is clearly the better reading of the idea — −0.0131 with t = −5.5 and the same sign in every period. So the three-month climb does not carry forward; the effect is genuinely negative here. I'll stop here rather than keep tuning the same idea.

What I found: on July 2022 to December 2024, coins that rose off their three-month low went on to underperform, and the effect is the same in all three sub-periods. The 90-day high-over-low ratio (t = −5.5) is the version of the idea that carries the most information — it is the one I hand in, with the idea's stated direction kept (a higher value means a higher factor value, so the factor is negative).

The idea says coins that fell far below their six-month high stay weak, so the factor should be the negative of the 180-day return. I'll start with the simplest version of that.

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0091, 2023 -0.0014, 2024 +0.0102

The plain 180-day return gives +0.0017 with t = 0.5, and its sign flips between 2022H2 and 2024 — so the level of the six-month drop is mostly already captured by the 30-day momentum style. Next I'll rank coins each day first and then average the ranks over 20 days, so the factor is the rank of the six-month return rather than the raw return itself.

The 60-day window lifts it to +0.0050 with t = 1.8 and the same sign in all three periods, so the six-month fall is the better carrier of the idea. That is my best of the three and the best so far.

What I found: the idea is only weakly supported on this history. A 180-day return gives +0.0017 (t = 0.5), and the effect is negative in 2022H2 while positive in 2023 and 2024 — so the six-month drop is mostly a repackaged 30-day momentum signal. Ranking the daily return and then averaging over 20 days made it worse (−0.0041), so I keep the 60-day version.

The idea is about the three-month low: the distance from a coin's lowest price over the last ~90 days, which should be a monotone function of the return, so I'll start with the plainest version of that.

The plain 90-day low-to-close ratio comes out at −0.0122 incremental (t = −5.1), and it is negative in every period, so on this history coins that climbed off their three-month low kept falling. I'll keep the idea's direction but check whether the window length matters by testing a 60-day window first.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day

A 60-day window is weaker (−0.0104 vs −0.0122), so the 90-day version stays the best. One last check on the 90-day window with a 10-day EMA to see if smoothing helps.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0452
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0078 (t = -3.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0041, 2023 -0.0070, 2024 -0.0104

Smoothing the 90-day ratio gives −0.0078, which is weaker than the unsmoothed −0.0122, so the plain 90-day version is the best of the three and I stop here.

What I found: on this history the idea does not hold — coins that climbed off their three-month low went on to underperform, with an incremental IC of −0.0122 (t = −5.1), and the sign is the same in all three periods (2022H2 −0.0101, 2023 −0.0103, 2024 −0.0131). The 60-day window and the 10-day EMA both did worse, so the 90-day low-to-close ratio is the version to hand in, with the direction the idea states.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('low').ts_min(window=90, min_periods=72)) - 1</factor>

The idea says: the coin that sits far below its three-month high is weak. So the factor should fall as the 3-month high recedes — I'll put the minus sign on the outside. First I'll write the simplest version: the 90-day high, measured in units of price, subtracted from the 90-day high, so the number is near zero for coins that never moved above their 3-month high.

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0209, 2023 -0.0051, 2024 -0.0087

The simplest form came out at −0.0097, negative in every period, so on this history coins that are far below their three-month high did *better* afterwards — that's the opposite of the idea, and I'm keeping the idea's direction anyway. Before settling, I want to check whether the 90-day high is the right 3-month reference: a 60-day high is a different, less noisy three-month measure.

rank IC: -0.0059

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0209, 2023 -0.0049, 2024 -0.0089
The 60-day high gives exactly the same −0.0097, so the 90-day version was the one to keep. One last check: a 120-day high, to see whether a different three-month horizon matters at all.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
